images.filename: 605-609 21st Street NW and 2031 F Street NW.jpg
images.caption: The former houses located at 605-609 21st Street NW and 2031 F Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C., were built in 1897 and designed by Arthur B. Heaton. The buildings are contributing properties to the George Washington University-Old West End Historic District. The building on the left is offices for The GW Hatchet.

images.caption: The Lenthall Houses (also known as the John Lenthall Houses) are located at 606 and 610 21st Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C. The Federal-style homes were built in 1800 by John Lenthall, principal assistant to Benjamin Latrobe during construction of the United States Capitol. They were originally located at 614 and 616 19th Street NW, but were moved in 1978 to prevent demolition (the old location is now occupied by one of the World Bank buildings). The Lenthall Houses are now owned by George Washington University and are listed on the National Register of Historic Places and District of Columbia Inventory of Historic Sites. They are also contributing properties to the George Washington University-Old West End Historic District.

images.caption: The Steedman-Ray House, now known as the F Street House, is located at 1925 F Street NW in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood of Washington, D.C. It serves as the residence of George Washington University's president. The house was constructed in 1849 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and the District of Columbia Inventory of Historic Sites. It is also a contributing property to the George Washington University-Old West End Historic District.

images.filename: Union Methodist Episcopal Church - Building XX.jpg
images.caption: Union Methodist Episcopal Church, now known as Building XX, is located at 814 20th Street NW in Washington, D.C. It was constructed in 1848 and expanded in 1910. During the Civil War the church served as a hospital for Union soldiers. It is a contributing property to the George Washington University/Old West End Historic District. The building served as a place of worship until 1975 and currently houses office space for George Washington University's Columbian College of Arts and Sciences.

images.caption: The building located at 1917 I Street NW (right) in Washington, D.C., constructed in 1892 as a private residence for Dr. James T. Sothoron, was designed by architect Paul J. Pelz. It was later the residence of William D. Hassett, a journalist and author who served as Secretary to the President for Franklin D. Roosevelt and Harry S. Truman, and office space for the National Federation of Business and Professional Women's Clubs. The building located at 1919 I Street NW was constructed in 1960.
